# Reception Perception: The Show — 2024-02-01

**Raw transcript:** `raw/ingested/reception-perception/2024-02-01-rp-arthur-smith-to-pittsburgh-seahawks-personnel-senior-bowl-takes.md` (immutable — do not edit)

## Summary

With co-host **James Koh** (not tracked). Same publication date as
[[Matt Waldman's RSP Cast - 2024-02-01]] but a different show entirely.
Three parts: the Arthur Smith hire in Pittsburgh (a coaching move this wiki
treats as high-durability, since it directly reshapes a specific receiver
room's usage), a round of coordinator-carousel resolutions, and early
3-game Reception Perception charting on three 2024 receiver prospects.

**Arthur Smith to Pittsburgh — the durable case.** Harmon (self-described
"the world's foremost and perhaps only Arthur Smith defender") separates
Smith's Atlanta *process* from its *results*: the underlying offensive
philosophy — heavy run-game commitment, funneling volume hard to a team's
best players (Derrick Henry's 300-carry seasons in Tennessee; no other
Titans back cleared 54 carries in 2019 or 50 in 2020; A.J. Brown/Corey Davis
combined for ~200 targets with no one else over 65), and route concepts
built around the middle of the field — was sound, and the failure was
Smith's own fit for a head-coaching chair, not the scheme. Direct charted
comparison: [[George Pickens]] ran dig/slant routes on just 7.7%/10.7% of
his snaps under Matt Canada in 2022, versus [[Drake London]]'s 16.6%/24.5%
under Arthur Smith the same year — offered as hard evidence of what
Pickens's route diet should look like once Smith calls plays instead of
Canada. New pages for [[George Pickens]], [[Najee Harris]], [[Jaylen Warren]] and [[Diontae Johnson]] — all directly affected by the scheme
change. See [[Scheme vs Talent]].

**Coordinator carousel, filtered for player relevance.** Both Ben Johnson
(Detroit) and Bobby Slowik (Houston) turned down head-coaching jobs and
stayed with their current teams — a real resolution (not just a further
firming, the opposite of the prior episode's rumor) of the standing "what
happens once Ben Johnson leaves" question hanging over [[Jared Goff]],
[[Amon-Ra St. Brown]] and [[Jameson Williams]]. Mike McDonald left Baltimore's
defensive coordinator role to become Seattle's head coach — filtered mostly
out as defense-only, except for real fantasy-relevant Seahawks-offense
speculation: doubt cast on [[Tyler Lockett]]'s roster spot given his cap
hit, and an expectation [[Jaxon Smith-Njigba]] moves into a bigger role.

**Early 2024 WR prospect charting (3-game samples, explicitly caveated as
too small to be held to).** [[Brian Thomas Jr.]] gets a full route-tree/
alignment breakdown — good vs. press, but a heavily concentrated route tree
(70% of routes are just three route types), a real X-receiver/Tee-Higgins-
bucket profile with a speculative Detroit fit floated. [[Keon Coleman]]
gets more skeptical detail — real separation questions, roughly 33rd
percentile early charting grade, and a direct Treylon Burks bust comp. New
page for [[Ladd McConkey]] — the strongest of the three on early tape,
excellent at selling vertical routes and snapping back on comebacks/outs, a
Cooper Kupp mold comp (with a real size caveat), Daniel Jeremiah's board
ranking him 44th overall. [[Quentin Johnston]] gets revisited as the
cautionary scheme-fit tale for grading any of these three.

## Not given pages

Allen Robinson and Calvin Austin (Pittsburgh depth-chart mentions only, no
evaluative content — Robinson likely cut, Austin "hasn't shown himself to
be a big-time target getter"), DK Metcalf and Zach Charbonnet (named only
as part of Seattle's existing talent inventory, no individual evaluative
claim), Devontae Parker (a recurring running joke/reference point for the
"generic average X receiver" archetype, not a evaluative claim about his
2024 outlook), Mike McDonald, Kyle Hamilton and other Baltimore/Seattle
defensive personnel (defense is out of scope for this wiki), Jahan Dotson,
Curtis Samuel, Dyami Brown and Byron Pringle (Washington receivers named
only dismissively as "not X receivers," no individual evaluation).
